subject: Turning an alcove into a workspace
hook: Is our alcove actually big enough to work at?
fb:
Bank holiday Monday question: is the alcove in our living room really big enough to work at?

It's one we hear a lot, and the answer is usually yes. A comfortable desk needs room for your laptop or screen, somewhere to rest your forearms, and clear space for your knees. Because a fitted desk is made to the exact width of the alcove and a depth that suits it, you often get more usable surface than a shop-bought desk would give you in the same spot.

If it won't work, we'll tell you straight. Ask us your question, or book a free consultation here:
https://superiofurniture.com/contact/?utm_source=facebook&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=productive-spaces-and-home-offices&utm_content=day-252
gbp:
Is my alcove big enough for a proper desk?

More often than people expect. A usable workspace needs three things: enough surface for a laptop or screen, room to rest your forearms, and clear knee space underneath. A made-to-measure desk is built to the exact width of the alcove and a depth that suits both the space and the way you work, so it often gives more usable surface than a standard desk squeezed into the same spot.

Shelving can be added above, set high enough to clear your head, with a cable route planned to the nearest socket. If the alcove is shallow, we can look at a desk that projects slightly beyond the chimney breast, or suggest another spot in the room.

We measure every alcove at several heights during the survey, because walls are rarely straight. If a desk won't work comfortably, we'll tell you honestly.

Book a free, no-obligation design consultation to find out what will fit.
